The inspected English book PDF contains the complete sentence on printed p. 122, with quotation marks around “Washing one’s hands.”

trail: The inspected book’s title and copyright pages identify Paulo Freire, translator Donaldo Macedo, and the 1985 English edition.

Printed page 122, in chapter 10, contains the sentence, using quotation marks to set off the opening metaphor. The surrounding argument rejects claims that churches and education are politically neutral.
Indiana University’s bibliography independently corroborates the English edition and translator. The claim is about this English text, not Freire’s use of English in a speech.

author.name: Paulo Freire
author.heading: About Paulo Freire
author.bio: Paulo Freire (1921–1997) was a Brazilian educator whose work connected literacy, dialogue and political participation. Best known for Pedagogy of the Oppressed, he treated education as a relationship in which learners actively interpret and change their world, rather than simply receive information.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: Freire’s chapter begins by treating churches as institutions within history, whose educational role cannot be understood abstractly. The quoted sentence states his objection to professed neutrality in a conflict shaped by unequal power. Its church-and-education setting gives the maxim a more specific argument than a generic instruction to take sides.
